dek: Tokopah Falls is the Sequoia National Park waterfall we cover. USGS calls it a 1,200-foot drop over granite. One $35 pass also covers Kings Canyon.
overview: Sequoia National Park, shared with Kings Canyon, is known for huge mountains, deep canyons and the largest trees.

Tokopah Falls is the waterfall we cover here. USGS describes a 1,200-foot drop over granite, and visitors have reviewed it. We don't have a published hike length for it. Tokopah is on the Marble Fork side of the park, not in Mineral King, so the Mineral King road dates don't apply to it.
fallsIntro: The height is the sourced fact. We don't have a hike length for Tokopah Falls, so confirm the distance and conditions with the park.
plan: No reservation is needed to drive in, and the same $35 pass covers Kings Canyon, so a Sequoia day and a Kings Canyon day can share one receipt. Rivers here are extremely hazardous in spring and early summer, when snowmelt is high, so check conditions before you go.
flow: The Marble Fork of the Kaweah River gauge near Lodgepole (USGS 11206820) is only about 0.6 mile from Tokopah Falls, on the same fork the USGS description mentions. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in June at about 100 cubic feet per second and was lowest in October at about 1.
Because it is on the same fork, it is a useful guide to when Tokopah Falls runs highest.
feesLead: It is the same pass as Kings Canyon, including the $100 per-person charge for non-US residents, and no entrance reservation is needed.
access: Winter storms can close roads until they are plowed. The park is otherwise open all day, all year. The weather page says the foothills can be in spring flower while Giant Forest still has snow, and that Mineral King and Cedar Grove are usually open to vehicles from late spring to early fall. Three Rivers is the gateway town for this side of the park, about 17 miles away in a straight line.
safety: The park says every river is extremely hazardous in spring and early summer because snowmelt makes the water cold and fast. We have no Tokopah-specific warnings on file.
